# Safety model

Every repository is reduced to exactly one **state**. Each operation then decides, per state, whether it may proceed or must skip with a reason.

## Repository states

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ready` | Clean, tracking, behind. The only state eligible for a default fast-forward update. |
| `current` | Clean and up to date with its upstream. |
| `dirty` | Uncommitted staged, unstaged, or untracked changes are present. |
| `in-progress` | A rebase, merge, cherry-pick, revert, or bisect is in progress. Never mutated. |
| `detached` | HEAD points at a commit rather than a branch. |
| `no-upstream` | The current branch has no tracking configuration. |
| `default-branch-unknown` | The default branch could not be inferred. Blocks default and sync. |
| `ambiguous-remote` | Several remotes exist and none is named 'origin'. Needs configuration. |
| `ahead` | Local commits are not on the remote; a fast-forward is not possible. |
| `diverged` | Local and upstream have both moved. Needs manual reconciliation. |
| `remote-unavailable` | A fetch failed, so remote state is unknown. Never guessed from stale refs. |

## Policy by operation

Generated by running the real decision functions over one representative snapshot per state.

| State | `update` | `default` | `sync` | `checkout` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ready` | proceed | proceed | proceed | proceed |
| `current` | proceed | proceed | proceed | proceed |
| `dirty` | skip | skip | skip | proceed |
| `in-progress` | skip | skip | skip | skip |
| `detached` | skip | skip | skip | proceed |
| `no-upstream` | skip | proceed | proceed | proceed |
| `default-branch-unknown` | proceed | skip | skip | proceed |
| `ambiguous-remote` | skip | skip | skip | proceed |
| `ahead` | skip | proceed | proceed | proceed |
| `diverged` | skip | proceed | proceed | proceed |
| `remote-unavailable` | skip | skip | skip | proceed |

> `checkout` is permissive by design: it only pre-skips an in-progress repository and a branch that exists nowhere. A dirty tree that would be overwritten is refused by git itself and reported as a failure.
